cases.sentence: Я прочитал у Ивана ___, что рыжие люди, если выпьют, – обязательно покраснеют…
cases.explain: The preposition «у» always governs the genitive, so Иван Бунин becomes Ивана Бунина.

cases.sentence: Опустит ноги в ледяную ___, нальет шампанского – и пишет.
cases.explain: «В» answering «куда?» (motion into something) takes the accusative; the feminine ванна becomes ванну.
The preposition «из» ('out of') is always followed by the genitive: из бокала.

cases.sentence: Модест Мусоргский лежит в ___ с перепою.
cases.explain: «В» answering «где?» (position, not direction) requires the prepositional case: в канаве.
The bare instrumental names the tool an action is performed with ('with his cane'), so no preposition is needed.

cases.sentence: Для чего это нужно было тайному ___ Гёте?
cases.explain: «Нужно» is impersonal: the person who needs something goes into the dative — тайному советнику.
It is the subject of the passive «была восстановлена», and subjects stand in the nominative.

cases.sentence: Просил ставить ему на ___ особый, розовый бокал.
cases.explain: «На» with motion (putting something onto a surface) takes the accusative; стол is inanimate, so its accusative looks like the nominative.

reading.question: Who starts the conversation in the carriage?
options: The black-moustached man in the jacket
reading.correct: The black-moustached man in the jacket
reading.explain: The man with the black moustache in a jacket speaks first, and addresses himself only to Venichka.

reading.ru: Я прочитал у Ивана Бунина, что рыжие люди, если выпьют, – обязательно покраснеют…
reading.question: What does the black-moustached man say he read in Ivan Bunin?
options: That red-haired people always go red when they drink
That drinking makes people go pale
That Bunin himself drank nothing but champagne
reading.correct: That red-haired people always go red when they drink
reading.explain: This is the first of his literary 'facts', and it opens the whole chain of writers-and-drink anecdotes.

reading.question: According to the storyteller, what did Chekhov add after saying 'Ich sterbe'?
reading.explain: In his telling, Chekhov said 'Ich sterbe', asked for champagne, and only then died.

reading.ru: Опустит ноги в ледяную ванну, нальет шампанского – и пишет.
reading.question: How is Friedrich Schiller said to have written?
options: With his feet in an icy bath and champagne poured out
Standing at a tall desk with beer
Only in the early morning, before drinking
reading.correct: With his feet in an icy bath and champagne poured out
reading.explain: The anecdote has Schiller writing with his feet in cold water and a glass of champagne at hand.

reading.ru: Пропустит пять бокалов – готова целая трагедия в пяти актах.
reading.question: What does five glasses of champagne produce, in the storyteller's arithmetic?
options: A whole tragedy in five acts
A single act of a tragedy
reading.correct: A whole tragedy in five acts
reading.explain: One glass gives one act, so five glasses give a complete five-act tragedy.

reading.question: What did Gogol supposedly do with the special glass he asked for at the Aksakovs'?
options: He drank out of the pink glass
He kept it empty on the table
He gave it to his host
reading.correct: He drank out of the pink glass
reading.explain: Gogol asked for a special pink glass and drank from it — vodka, the storyteller assumes.

reading.ru: Модест на лавочке похмелиться хочет: что ему ноты!
reading.question: What is Mussorgsky thinking about while he sits writing his notes?
options: Getting a hair of the dog rather than the music
Finishing the opera as fast as he can
reading.correct: Getting a hair of the dog rather than the music
reading.explain: He wants a drink to cure his hangover, and the notes mean nothing to him — but Rimsky-Korsakov will not let him.

reading.question: What does the black-moustached man say about books and his own drinking?
options: He loves reading, but a good book depresses him and sends him back to drink
He never reads anything at all
He only reads when he is sober for a whole year
He reads instead of drinking and is proud of it
reading.correct: He loves reading, but a good book depresses him and sends him back to drink
reading.explain: He drinks for a month or two, reads a book, finds himself vile beside it, throws the book away and starts drinking again.

reading.ru: Все ценные люди России, все нужные ей люди – все пили, как свиньи.
reading.question: What is his claim about Russia's valuable and necessary people?
options: They all drank like pigs, while the useless ones did not drink
They drank only champagne, never vodka
reading.correct: They all drank like pigs, while the useless ones did not drink
reading.explain: He divides Russians into the valuable drinkers and the superfluous, muddle-headed non-drinkers.

reading.ru: Ему еще в Храпунове надо было выходить, этому Герцену, а он все едет, собака…
reading.question: What does the man in the covercoat coat shout about Herzen?
options: That Herzen should have got off at Khrapunovo but is still riding along
That Herzen never drank a drop
That Herzen is asleep in the next carriage
That Herzen is going all the way to Petushki with them
reading.correct: That Herzen should have got off at Khrapunovo but is still riding along
reading.explain: He takes the phrase about 'waking Herzen' literally and treats Herzen as a passenger who has missed his stop.

reading.ru: Вот тайный советник Гёте, например, совсем не пил.
reading.question: What counter-example does the decembrist offer against all this drinking?
options: Privy Councillor Goethe, who did not drink at all
reading.correct: Privy Councillor Goethe, who did not drink at all
reading.explain: He interrupts to ask whether one cannot simply pull oneself together, and names Goethe as proof that one can.

reading.ru: Так он, чтобы самому не скопытиться, вместо себя заставлял пить всех своих персонажей.
reading.question: How does Venichka explain Goethe's sobriety?
options: Goethe made his characters drink in his place so as not to go under himself
Goethe was simply never offered anything
Goethe replaced wine with icy baths
reading.correct: Goethe made his characters drink in his place so as not to go under himself
reading.explain: Venichka's rescue of the argument: in Faust everybody drinks, because Goethe delegated his drinking to his characters.

reading.ru: Он остался жить, но как бы покончил с собой.
reading.question: What does Venichka say Goethe achieved by having Werther shoot himself?
options: He stayed alive while in effect committing suicide
He made his readers kill themselves instead
He proved that he was braver than his characters
reading.correct: He stayed alive while in effect committing suicide
reading.explain: Venichka calls this worse than a real suicide — more cowardice, egoism and creative baseness.

reading.ru: А все потому, что в Есино нет пассажиров, они все садятся или в Храпунове, или во Фрязеве.
reading.question: In Venichka's parable, why does the train never stop at Yesino?
options: Because there are no passengers there — they all board at Khrapunovo or Fryazevo
Because the station has been closed
Because the driver has been drinking
Because everyone in Yesino is going the other way
reading.correct: Because there are no passengers there — they all board at Khrapunovo or Fryazevo
reading.explain: People walk from Yesino to the next stations because they know the train will race through Yesino anyway — the same circular logic Venichka applies to Goethe.

reading.question: What happens once Venichka has rebuilt the black-moustached man's theory?
options: The bottles come out and the drinking starts again
The decembrist gets off the train
They begin arguing about Herzen once more
reading.correct: The bottles come out and the drinking starts again
reading.explain: The decembrist produces a bottle of pepper vodka and the black-moustached man his Stolichnaya, and they all rub their hands.

reading.ru: Итак, за здоровье тайного советника Иоганна фон Гёте?
reading.question: What toast does the chapter end on?
options: To the health of Privy Councillor Johann von Goethe
To the health of Anton Chekhov
To Herzen, who is still riding
reading.correct: To the health of Privy Councillor Johann von Goethe
reading.explain: Having just been proved a secret drunkard, Goethe becomes the subject of the company's toast.

highlight.question: Which sentence reports what Chekhov asked for after saying 'Ich sterbe'?
sentences: – Как, то есть «ну, а дальше»?
Последние, предсмертные слова Антона Чехова какие были?
Он сказал: «Ихь штербе», то есть «я умираю».
А потом добавил: «Налейте мне шампанского».
И уж тогда только – умер.
highlight.explain: The fourth sentence is the request for champagne that follows the German words.

highlight.question: Which sentence describes the posture Schiller supposedly wrote in?
sentences: – А Фридрих Шиллер – тот не только умереть, тот даже жить не мог без шампанского.
Он знаете как писал?
Опустит ноги в ледяную ванну, нальет шампанского – и пишет.
Пропустит один бокал – готов целый акт трагедии.
Пропустит пять бокалов – готова целая трагедия в пяти актах.
highlight.explain: Only the third sentence describes the icy bath and the poured champagne.

highlight.question: Which sentence says that Rimsky-Korsakov would not let Mussorgsky have a drink?
sentences: И вот они сидят – Николай Римский-Корсаков в креслах сидит, закинув ногу за ногу, с цилиндром на отлете.
А напротив него – Модест Мусоргский, весь томный, весь небритый – пригнувшись на лавочке, потеет и пишет ноты.
Модест на лавочке похмелиться хочет: что ему ноты!
А Николай Римский-Корсаков с цилиндром на отлете похмелиться не дает…
highlight.explain: The last sentence is the refusal; the one before it only says that Modest wants a drink.

highlight.question: Which sentence names the man the decembrist puts forward as someone who did not drink at all?
sentences: – Стоп! – прервал его декабрист.
– А разве нельзя не пить?
Взять себя в руки – и не пить?
Вот тайный советник Гёте, например, совсем не пил.
highlight.explain: Goethe is named only in the final sentence of the interruption.

highlight.question: Which sentence says what the decembrist pulled out of his covercoat coat?
sentences: – Вот это да-а-а… – восторженно разглядывали меня и декабрист, и черноусый.
Стройная система была восстановлена, и вместе с ней восстановилось веселье.
Декабрист – широким жестом – вытащил из коверкотового пальто бутылку перцовой и поставил ее у ног черноусого.
Черноусый вынул свою столичную.
Все потирали руки – до странности возбужденно…
highlight.explain: The third sentence is the one about the bottle of pepper vodka taken from the coat.

highlight.question: Which sentence describes what the young Mitrich did when he was handed a glass?
sentences: Мне налили – больше всех.
Старому Митричу – тоже налили.
Молодому тоже подали стакан – он радостно прижал его к левому соску правым бедром, и из обеих ноздрей его хлынули слезы…
highlight.explain: The last sentence describes him pressing the glass to his left nipple with his right thigh and weeping from both nostrils.
